question: Does the registered state-space verifier establish strict continuous-time Hurwitz stability and solve the actual requested symmetric Lyapunov equation independently of numerical time scales and the sign of Q?
input_semantics: Existing float parsing followed by exact rational interpretation of the accepted finite binary64 values. B/C, rank arithmetic and transfer-function mode stay outside this repair.

output_contract.hurwitz_stable: Exact identity-Q Lyapunov criterion: true iff its symmetric solution is unique and strictly positive definite.
output_contract.lyapunov_P_exact: Matrix of exact rational strings for a unique requested-Q solution; null otherwise.
output_contract.lyapunov_P: Matrix of floats if all exact entries have finite non-underflowed float representations; null otherwise.
output_contract.lyapunov_pd: Exact strict positive definiteness for a unique requested solution; null for inconsistent/nonunique equations.
output_contract.lyapunov_residual_exact: True for a unique solution independently satisfying every exact equation entry; null otherwise.

stability_certificate.P_exact: Identity-Q rational solution matrix or null

output_contract.passed: Valid systems with a verified unique/inconsistent/nonunique requested equation can pass without requiring stability or positive requested P. Retain existing characteristic-polynomial residual check. Invalid Q explicitly refuses.
output_contract.undefined_pd_claim: Either Boolean claimed value explicitly refuses with a reason; never float(null), never treat an undefined PD flag as false.
output_contract.invalid_Q: Wrong shape, nonfinite, or nonsymmetric Q explicitly refuses; symmetric positive, zero, semidefinite and indefinite Q are valid.

families.name: nonsymmetric_Q
families.expected: Explicit refused request; no solver exception or substituted symmetric RHS.

families.name: identity_nonunique
families.proof: Identity equation fixes diagonal(1/2,-1/2), leaves off-diagonal free; no positive-definite solution.

families.name: coordinate_and_time
families.proof: Signed permutations and dyadic diagonal scaling preserve every supplied binary64 coefficient.

claim_checks: Every system is called unclaimed and with False/True for each of hurwitz_stable and lyapunov_pd. Unique valid results accept exactly the truthful value. Singular valid equations accept exactly the truthful stability claim, and refuse both undefined-PD claims. Invalid Q refuses all four claims.
oracles: Compare exact returned requested P strings to stated analytical P as rational numbers; no floating tolerance can convert a nonzero expected entry to zero.
Verify every returned exact requested and identity certificate against all entries of A^T P+PA using rational arithmetic of the supplied floats; this receiver does not solve a linear system.
Check strict PD of the returned 1x1/2x2 certificate by its diagonal/principal determinant, and match the known spectrum for Hurwitz flags.

For representable unique P entries require numerical matrix agreement within relative1e-12, with exact zeros checked as zero. Unrepresentable unique matrices are null and keep the lossless rational solution.
Require allow_nan=false JSON serialization and no exceptions for all32 systems and128 claims.
Registered Pi representative cases: mixed stable defaultQ, slow unstable control, and coupled semidefiniteQ; include defined and undefined Boolean claim handling.
Run every inherited repository CI gate, including merged rank159's analytical and real Pi checks.
decision: All32 classifications/requested-solution/certificate/range checks and128 Boolean claim outcomes correct, zero exceptions, real Pi and full maintained CI success. Preserve all original stock outcomes; no coefficient/tolerance or case changes after first execution.
execution: Native source preparation only, then one matched stock/candidate pair through maintained pull_request CI. No local numerical execution, no unsupported dispatcher retry, organizer data, dev-set run, scored submission, or paid model call.

references.sections: Lecture 14, Theorem 14.1: continuous-time Lyapunov equivalence and uniqueness
Slides 9-10 and 9-19: Lyapunov solvability and continuous-time Hurwitz criterion
